orgDesign.companyProfile: Amsterdam-based bookkeeping-as-a-service company modeled on Kees de Boekhouder (founded 2009 by Kees Monteban and Marlou ter Berg at Nieuwe Teertuinen 25A, with offices in Rotterdam at Stationsplein 45 and Utrecht at Oudegracht 27) after Vortex Capital Partners took a stake in the buyout announced on 24-25 May 2022, when the company served 6,500+ clients. Today it serves more than 10,000 entrepreneurs throughout the Netherlands with roughly 100 staff - bookkeepers, marketers, IT and HR - of whom about 40 percent are internally trained bookkeepers; the organisation is modeled at about 115 people including the sister company Founders (Founders Finance B.V., founded 2018, same address) that serves holding and operating BVs. The proposition is a proprietary web and mobile application plus a personal bookkeeper on a fixed yearly fee invoiced monthly: eenmanszaak EUR 840, VOF EUR 1,140 for two partners plus EUR 100 per extra partner, holding BV EUR 1,750 and werkmaatschappij EUR 2,450 (all ex VAT), with add-ons for the Ponto bank connection (EUR 5 per month per account), the partner income tax return (EUR 125 incl. VAT) and payroll (EUR 17.50 per payslip per employee per month). Kees Monteban (CEO and co-founder; Rogier van den Heuvel is listed as CEO on the 2026 team page) leads with COO Rody Turpijn and heads of QA, Growth, Operations, Finance and People; Vortex partner Joost Moerland sponsors the thesis of a loyal customer base that becomes brand ambassadors, a revenue CAGR above 25 percent, a growth target of 20,000 clients, and the professionalisation of the technology function - so that the brand becomes the go-to bookkeeper for freelancers.
orgDesign.operatingModel: With about 115 people the company is a service organisation with a small product and engineering function inside it, not a software vendor with a support desk: three groups and twelve teams. Bookkeeping Operations is the largest group by far - bookkeeping pods of internally trained bookkeepers and team leads in Amsterdam, Rotterdam and Utrecht, each bookkeeper carrying a personal portfolio of clients and backed up by colleagues, a quality and tax-knowledge team under the Head of QA that runs four-eyes checks, internal training and the advice knowledge base, and the Founders bookkeepers who serve BVs at the same fixed-fee model. Product and Engineering, professionalised since the Vortex investment, is seven small teams of full-stack developers and solution architects of three to five people each: stream-aligned teams own the client app, receipts and banking, invoicing and the bookkeeper workspace; a complicated-subsystem team owns the ledger, VAT, year-end and income tax logic that encodes Dutch fiscal rules; and two platform teams provide identity, audit trail and AVG compliance and the Belastingdienst, KVK, Ponto and payment integrations. Growth and Client Success, under the Head of Growth and the client success lead, owns the funnel from website and partner referral to the free Google Meet intro, the mutual-fit check, onboarding, bookkeeper matching, the switch from a previous bookkeeper, subscription billing and retention. Because the bookkeepers and client success executives are themselves customers of the platform (bkpr and csux), every friction in a review queue, a Scan & Herken miss or a bank re-authorisation reaches the product teams within the same building; the workspace team plans bookkeeper capacity as a product so that clients per bookkeeper can grow toward 20,000 clients without losing the personal relationship that the brand is built on. Every team is steward of the data assets its bricks create, so the client administration, the filed returns and the advice knowledge base stay coherent and AVG-compliant as the company scales.

This is the technology function that Vortex set out to professionalise, and its job is to raise clients served per bookkeeper while making administration take almost no time for clients.
